awarding_body.detail: The page is the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science's own page for the AEF Program and states that WDTS manages the programme for DOE in collaboration with ORISE, matching the record's awarding body.
awarding_body.quote: The DOE Office of Science's Office of Workforce Development for Teachers and Scientists (WDTS) manages this program for DOE in collaboration with the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) and other partners.

deadline.detail: The current cycle is open: the main page announces applications are due November 5, 2026 at 8:00pm ET, and the Key Dates page gives the same deadline with the online application opening of August 3, 2026. Today (12 October 2026) the deadline is in the future, so the cycle is currently open.
deadline.quote: The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship Program is now open for applications. Applications are due November 5, 2026 at 8:00pm ET.

eligibility.detail: All six record claims are confirmed verbatim on the Eligibility page: U.S. citizenship; five complete years of full-time classroom teaching; five of the last seven years full-time in a public or private elementary or secondary school in a STEM discipline; current full-time employment; ability to obtain an eleven-month leave of absence; and a recommendation letter from a school district official.
eligibility.quote: Be a U.S. citizen at the time of applying (by the November 5, 2026 application deadline).

funding.detail: The record's 'Stipend' funding type is accurate. Fellows receive a monthly living stipend of $8,200, plus a travel allowance up to $5,000, an education allowance up to $1,000, relocation reimbursement up to $3,500, and a health-insurance stipend of up to $550/month (individual) or $1,300/month (family). There is no tuition element because this is not a degree programme.
funding.quote: Receives a monthly living stipend of $8,200.

degree_levels.detail: Confirmed as a non-degree professional fellowship for K-12 STEM educators: fellows spend eleven months serving in Federal agencies or U.S. Congressional offices; no academic degree is awarded.
degree_levels.quote: The Albert Einstein Distinguished Educator Fellowship (AEF) Program provides a unique opportunity for accomplished K-12 educators in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) to serve in the national education arena.

recommended_field_updates.deadline_text: Application Deadline: 8:00pm Eastern, November 5, 2026 (On-line Application opened August 3, 2026)
recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Confirmed live on 2026-10-12 against science.osti.gov/wdts/einstein and its Eligibility, Benefits and Key Dates subpages. Next re-check (expected around August 2027): the cycle is annual, the online application opens in early August and the deadline is in early November (the Key Dates page header labels the current process 2027-2028, while its orientation line still reads 2026-2027 - a known quirk of the official page; the deadline itself is unambiguous). Stipend and allowance amounts are set annually and may change; re-read the Benefits page rather than copying the 2026-2027 figures. The record's deadline_label idiom 'typically opens in mid-August, with applications due in mid-November' is looser than the published dates (opens August 3, due November 5) and could be tightened to the official wording.
